papers.summary: Introduces spectral weight decay as a decoupled nuclear-norm update that shrinks singular values additively. It lowers effective rank and improves compression, inference speed, and robustness to label noise relative to standard weight decay.
papers.relevance: Direct match for spectral regularization, effective rank, low-rank compressibility, and memorization under label noise.

evidence.quote: Across LLaMA models with 124 M to 500 M parameters, spectral weight decay lowers effective rank and improves SVD-LLM compression at matched validation loss.
At 500 M and a 4% distortion budget, it reaches 1.89× compression and a 1.18× GPU inference speedup, compared with 1.14× and 1.01× after standard weight decay.

papers.title: Spectral Weight Decay: Inducing Low-Rank Structure in Neural Network Weights

papers.summary: Proposes sMuon, a matmul-only approximation of Muon for LoRA updates. It evaluates the method across four models and eleven SFT benchmarks, plus ReLoRA pretraining, finding model-dependent gains and a joint-best validation loss with Riemannion.
papers.relevance: Directly addresses optimization geometry for LoRA, Muon, spectral behavior, and efficient low-rank pretraining.

evidence.quote: We provide a matmul-only algorithm of the method, sMuon, that is efficient for modern hardware, with comparable speed to other Muon methods ... while being significantly faster than Riemannion for larger LoRA rank.
In the ReLoRA pretraining setting, we illustrate that Muon LoRA methods are generally stronger than AdamW LoRA.

papers.title: Approximate Muon with low-rank adapters

papers.summary: Introduces NoRA, which normalizes LoRA down-projection matrices during training or only at initialization. The abstract reports improved convergence, performance, stability, and reduced catastrophic forgetting across pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning.
papers.relevance: Strong match for LoRA training dynamics, regularization, convergence, and practical parameter-efficient fine-tuning.

evidence.quote: We introduce Normalized Low-Rank Adaptation (NoRA), a simple yet effective method that normalizes the down-projection matrices during training.
Across pretraining, supervised finetuning, and reinforcement learning, NoRA consistently accelerates convergence, improves performance and training stability, and mitigates catastrophic forgetting.

papers.title: Normalized Low-Rank Adaptation

papers.summary: Proposes NorMuon, combining Muon's orthogonalization with neuron-wise adaptive normalization and an efficient distributed FSDP2 implementation. It targets optimizer conditioning, balanced parameter updates, and scalable training.
papers.relevance: Relevant to optimizer design, Newton-Schulz-style orthogonalization, distributed implementation, and training-efficiency tradeoffs at scale.

evidence.quote: NorMuon addresses this imbalance by maintaining second-order momentum statistics for each neuron and applying row-wise normalization after orthogonalization.
To enable practical deployment at scale, we develop an efficient distributed implementation under the FSDP2 framework.

papers.title: NorMuon: Making Muon more efficient and scalable

papers.summary: Introduces Context Language Models that manage context as an editable file and evaluates model-controlled context management across browsing, long-horizon, and multi-agent tasks. The abstract reports improved accuracy and lower compute than external context-management strategies.
papers.relevance: Directly relevant to the user's research-digest agent, context management, and application-controlled orchestration interests.

evidence.quote: We introduce Context Language Models (CLMs), language models that natively manage their own context.
Building CLMs zero-shot with existing models outperforms SOTA context management strategies across a variety of tasks: 11.4% higher accuracy with 21.5% fewer FLOPs on BrowseComp-Plus.

papers.title: Context Language Models
